1902.report: Independent review of PR #1902 (f44e2fd78..f1169ba01) against Issue #1898. The diff is only deploy/acl-hub/** (7 files, +447/-2). Its patch-id (fc24e3b6) is the same as the earlier heads 61c7f3d9c and 1cf7a5664, which was reviewed line by line. Migration 0008 adds users and account_assignments (account_name COLLATE NOCASE, soft removed_at, index on user_email+removed_at) with no proxy or tracking columns. POST /v1/session checks the token with Google tokeninfo. It refuses an unverified email, a domain outside ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, an azp/aud other than GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and a disabled user. Google 5xx or a network failure gives 503 and a rejected token 401. A valid token returns a 30-day key <email>.<exp>.<HMAC-SHA256 USER_KEY_SECRET>. The Google token is never stored (src/users.js:48-76). The user key is parsed from the right, so it is unambiguous; expiry is enforced, the compare is constant-time via sameSecret (src/auth.js:21) and the disabled flag is checked on every request (src/users.js:26-35). GET /v1/my-accounts returns only the caller's rows, including removed ones, with an ETag/304 (src/users.js:79-88). GET /api/users, POST /api/assignments and POST /api/assignments/remove require the owner (OWNER_KEY bearer or the SameSite=Strict owner cookie) or a non-disabled admin user. Without auth they return 401, a buyer gets 403. POST /api/users/role needs OWNER_KEY only (first-admin bootstrap) (src/users.js:164-177). All SQL is parameterized. Assignment rows are allowlisted, so unknown, proxy and tracking fields return 400 with nothing written; the upsert runs in one DB.batch. Remove is a soft update and never deletes. Non-blocking nit: removeAssignments does not check for '@' in user_email (src/users.js:144). Tests: node --test test/users.test.js test/schema.test.js 16/16 pass. main is still 4c63ef0c; the PR base is 4c63ef0c and the PR is MERGEABLE. The diff vs main has 22 files, 1768-only: no targeting_resolver.py / test_acl1771 changes, so the 1771 code now comes from main.

### Merge 74eb343a vs my merge notes
I rebuilt my resolved trial tree (main + my resolution) and compared it with 74eb343a. The `src` difference is limited to a removed comment, the order of the copy_more/file_vertical lines in app.py, and an en-dash in a JS comment. tests/test_acl1819_preflight.py adds the new 2-ad-set texts_dynamic parity fixtures. Every note is applied:
- texts_dynamic counts `st["ads"]` in Python and `st.ads` in JS;
- the Primary-text-2 RPA refusal is dropped;
- TermResolver gets cache/scope; API_ONLY_SLOT_KEYS is the union of both sides;
- FUTURE = placements + copyTo; `_targeting_body` is defined once;
- 1774's more_copy_names/vertical_filename are set per ad set.

### Blockers from round 2: fixed
1. **Targeting reads.** `estimate_targeting_reads` = min(90, 6 + 6 × distinct terms and parts across all sets) is added to the per-campaign budget. The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. With 4 terms per set the resolver cap is hit and the run is refused before any write ("press Check plan again"); this is 1771 behaviour. 2 sets × 3 terms: success.
2. **ACL-1891.** `_prepare` refuses before the first write when `chunk_calls + estimate_create_calls(plan) > budget`. Check plan (`writing=False`) keeps the old reserve. The 1891 test is rewritten and a new test is added; the 1891 suite passes.

### Non-blocking items from round 2: done
- The pixel guard is dropped.
- Targeting of all ad sets is resolved before one combined TargetingUnresolved is raised.
- A comment now covers creative numbering.
- The changelog covers the v3-page downgrade.

### Remaining notes (non-blocking, no re-review needed)
- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. The likely cause is a transient Windows file-sharing error (AV/indexer) on `os.replace` or `_read`.
  - It does expose a real 1771 robustness gap, so I suggest a follow-up task for 1771 (not this PR):
    - `_read` maps any OSError, including PermissionError, to `{}`, and the next `put` would then rewrite the file with only the new entry, dropping the confirmed cache;
    - `os.replace` is not retried.
  - Fix: on a read error other than file-not-found, refuse to write or retry, and retry the replace on PermissionError.

review.report: Independent review of PR #1902 (f44e2fd78..f1169ba01) against Issue #1898. The diff is only deploy/acl-hub/** (7 files, +447/-2). Its patch-id (fc24e3b6) is the same as the earlier heads 61c7f3d9c and 1cf7a5664, which was reviewed line by line. Migration 0008 adds users and account_assignments (account_name COLLATE NOCASE, soft removed_at, index on user_email+removed_at) with no proxy or tracking columns. POST /v1/session checks the token with Google tokeninfo. It refuses an unverified email, a domain outside ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, an azp/aud other than GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and a disabled user. Google 5xx or a network failure gives 503 and a rejected token 401. A valid token returns a 30-day key <email>.<exp>.<HMAC-SHA256 USER_KEY_SECRET>. The Google token is never stored (src/users.js:48-76). The user key is parsed from the right, so it is unambiguous; expiry is enforced, the compare is constant-time via sameSecret (src/auth.js:21) and the disabled flag is checked on every request (src/users.js:26-35). GET /v1/my-accounts returns only the caller's rows, including removed ones, with an ETag/304 (src/users.js:79-88). GET /api/users, POST /api/assignments and POST /api/assignments/remove require the owner (OWNER_KEY bearer or the SameSite=Strict owner cookie) or a non-disabled admin user. Without auth they return 401, a buyer gets 403. POST /api/users/role needs OWNER_KEY only (first-admin bootstrap) (src/users.js:164-177). All SQL is parameterized. Assignment rows are allowlisted, so unknown, proxy and tracking fields return 400 with nothing written; the upsert runs in one DB.batch. Remove is a soft update and never deletes. Non-blocking nit: removeAssignments does not check for '@' in user_email (src/users.js:144). Tests: node --test test/users.test.js test/schema.test.js 16/16 pass. The full node --test is 127/130; the same 3 test/report.test.js tests (live levels and text, live filters by manager, object errors are shown as text) fail identically on clean main 1e525327b (time-dependent fixtures), so they are not caused by this PR. PR CI at f1169ba01 is green. Deploy is out of scope (wrangler.toml has placeholders only).

Independent review of ACL-2491 (Issue 1491), PR #1492, by Reviewer-R1121A (session r1121a-acl2491-s1). Verdict: APPROVED with non-blocking follow-ups.
Scope checked: full diff 82d13d82..444f3a60 (creator.py, graph.py, targeting_resolver.py, publish_api.py, test_acl1771, changelog). Both resolver constructions in publish_api pass the ad account (self.act / sess.act); the act is validated as act_<digits>, so a malformed value turns the extra search off. GET /{act}/targetingsearch?q=term&limit=50 (one page) runs only after an adinterest miss (the exact adinterestvalid hit and the adinterest exact/tail hit return first). Only rows with type interests/behaviors are used; probed work_employers/life_events/rows without type are ignored (term stays unresolved). A permission refusal is an optional-lookup refusal: one English warning, no ids. Reads only, no POST. Cache keys for /search are unchanged; targetingsearch keys are prefixed with the path. _read_context reports operation=targetingsearch.
Checks: tests/test_acl1771_targeting_resolver.py, test_acl1920_optional_refusals.py, test_acl1886_graph_error_context.py, test_acl2105_profile_pages.py -> 172 passed. GitHub CI on head 444f3a60: all required jobs pass (linux 1/2/3, windows, ACL verification, installer verification, descriptor, tracker-link, process instructions); macOS smoke and the build/install job are skipped by path classification.
Finding (1), read budget, reproduced with a simulation: JOB_READ_PER_TERM stays 6 but a term found nowhere now costs 7 reads when adinterest reads 2 pages; with 5 or more such terms one term becomes 'unknown' and Check plan says "Couldn't check all interests — press Check plan again" (with 1 adinterest page there is no unknown up to 8 terms). Not blocking: the budget exists to cap reads per job on a live account, and the cap holds; the overflow is loud, never a wrong pick, and the shared plan cache lets the next Check plan continue.
Follow-ups (non-blocking): (1) +1 to the per-term job budget when act is set; (2) a non-permission error from targetingsearch (e.g. code 100) fails Check plan as other optional lookups do (confirmed: GraphError [lookup=targetingsearch]); a fallback search might better degrade to a warning; (3) if live rows lack type, the feature silently does nothing - the live capture must confirm type=interests; (4) missing tests: row-type filtering, budget with several unfound terms, _read_context for targetingsearch.
Live capture required from the owner: raw targetingsearch response for 'Creative real estate investing' (id masked) showing rows with id/name/type=interests; Check plan shows the term exact; a second Check plan keeps it exact (the warm entry must survive the adinterestvalid id re-check).

No timers, prompts, buttons or banners added; sync triggers unchanged. seed_rows (user_accounts.py:401-425) sends only account_name + SERVER_FIELDS, skips rows hidden on this machine (hidden_accounts) and duplicate names: consistent with 'current map' as the buyer sees it; merge_into_map with an empty server list hides nothing, so a failed seed cannot drop the map. Independent review of PR #1910 (8969b2c09..c4cd5f2bd) against Issue #1901 (accounts per user 4/4). Hub: POST /v1/my-accounts/seed (deploy/acl-hub/src/users.js:95-118) requires a valid user key (401 otherwise), reuses validRows/ROW_FIELDS so proxy_* and tracking_link give 400, caps 2000 rows, returns 409 if the user has any assignment row including removed ones, inserts rows with assigned_by='seed' via INSERT..SELECT WHERE NOT EXISTS(non-seed row) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a seed never overwrites existing rows and an admin assignment that lands between check and insert blocks the seed. Two machines of the same user seeding at once: both may pass the 409 check; result is the union of both maps as seed rows, nothing overwritten (acceptable, both maps belong to the user). Routing in index.js:52, README row added. ACL: src/web/user_accounts.py:353-370 seeds only when GET /v1/my-accounts returned an empty list and the user email (parsed from the key, matching hub key format <email>.<exp>.<hmac>) is not in seeded_for; then re-reads my-accounts without ETag. Failure (unreachable or non-200/409) returns None and clears the stored ETag so the next event-driven sync retries; 409 and empty map are final. No timers, prompts, buttons or banners added; sync triggers unchanged. seed_rows (user_accounts.py:401-425) sends only account_name + SERVER_FIELDS, skips rows hidden on this machine (hidden_accounts) and duplicate names: consistent with 'current map' as the buyer sees it; merge_into_map with an empty server list hides nothing, so a failed seed cannot drop the map. User key never logged (log lines carry only status/counts). Acceptance: 1) empty user seeded without proxy/tracking - test_empty_user_gets_map_seeded_without_proxy_or_tracking, hub seed.test.js; 2) user with assignments not re-seeded, hub 409 - test_user_with_assignments_is_not_seeded, test_hub_refusal_409_is_final, seed.test.js 409 tests; 3) once, no click - test_seed_happens_once_per_user; 4) tests on both sides. Tests: node --test in deploy/acl-hub 137 tests, 134 pass, 3 fail = known report.test.js failures on main (live filters by manager, live levels and text, object errors are shown as text); seed.test.js 7/7 pass. pytest tests/test_acl2899_user_accounts.py tests/test_acl2901_first_signin_seed.py = 29 passed. CI on c4cd5f2bd all green (linux 1-3, windows, tracker-link, descriptor, process instructions, installer classification). Non-blocking: rows with NULL assigned_by would not block the seed's NOT EXISTS guard (admin path always sets assigned_by).

Independent review of PR #1908 (f44e2fd78..9c5bff140) against Issue #1907. GitHubBackend._call now raises 'GitHub is unreachable: <reason>. Try again when the connection is restored.' with reason from new _network_reason(): SSLCertVerificationError/CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED -> certificate verification failed; timeouts -> timed out; gaierror/getaddrinfo -> DNS lookup failed; 'Tunnel connection failed' or ConnectionRefusedError -> proxy refused (if an https proxy is configured or tunnel text) else connection refused; else 'other: <text>' where URLs are replaced by [url], the token is replaced by [redacted], whitespace collapsed, capped at 120 chars. Redaction precedes truncation; headers are never read; the request URL is never included (only the exception reason). No-leak: verified in all branches including other. Messages reach UI unchanged: Target/Ad titles/Forms/Add error lines and connection_settings diagnostic line use str(LibraryError) (diagnostic line additionally replaces token); no UI rewrap. TLS criterion: team_library uses plain urllib.request.urlopen, release_updates uses build_opener(_NoRedirect)+urlopen, both default HTTPSHandler with system store; no SSLContext/certifi anywhere in src/web or team_library, so trust setup is identical. PUT path still raises WriteUncertain without reason: acceptable (message is intentionally about an uncertain save; the preceding GET reads show the reason; adding a reason there would be nice-to-have, non-blocking). Owner rules: no new retries, timers, buttons, banners; English text. Non-blocking nit: any non-verify ssl.SSLError (handshake) falls to 'other: ...'. Tests: tests/test_team_library.py 50 passed (7 parametrized reasons, proxy-configured refusal, no-secret test). Re-review after base refresh to 8969b2c09 (head 37eaabda8): patch-id of the diff unchanged; CI green.
